newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nikkei average's biggest drops in the past.
newsitem.headline: Nikkei average's biggest drops in the past.

text.p: The 4.26 percent fall in the Nikkei share index of 225 leading shares on Friday was not among the 10 largest in the Tokyo market's history.
The biggest drop ever came on October 20, 1987, the day after the "Black Monday" plunge on Wall Street.
The second-largest fall registered on March 5, 1953, was prompted by worries over Soviet leader Joseph Stalin's declining health.
The Nikkei stock average was introduced at the Tokyo Stock Exchange in 1932.
The index's all-time high of 38,915.87 points was registered on December 29, 1989, when the Japanese economy was at the height of an economic bubble of inflated asset prices.
